summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis and cirrhosis was admitted with melena and general malaise. She had a drop in hemoglobin from 9.9 to 8.3 and was found to have ongoing gastrointestinal bleeding. She received one unit of packed red blood cells, with a mild transfusion reaction managed with Benadryl. She underwent urgent endoscopy, which revealed grade III esophageal varices with stigmata of recent bleeding; three bands were placed. She remained hemodynamically stable but required a second unit of blood due to persistent melena. She was treated with octreotide and IV proton pump inhibitor, later transitioned to oral pantoprazole. Sucralfate and ciprofloxacin were started for mucosal healing and infection prophylaxis. Her abdominal pain and itching improved with supportive care. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans for follow-up endoscopy and colonoscopy, and instructions to monitor for recurrent bleeding.
problems: Esophageal varices in diseases classified elsewhere, with bleeding
